key_decisions.decision: Preserves the exact kinship and the legal reason for purchase.
Keeps both property rights and the recognition that follows the visit.
Combines seven and ten into seventeen without changing the weight or introducing coins.
Preserves all four formal actions and the weighed payment.
Makes the legal-document construction readable while retaining sealed and open forms.
Retains Baruch's two generations; renders the anomalous kinship term broadly and documents the literal uncle/cousin discrepancy.
Keeps the public nature of the instruction.
Preserves both documents, earthenware storage, and the stated preservation purpose.
Uses the established Lord GOD convention for Adonai plus the divine name and preserves the creation appeal.
Retains both faithful love and the difficult intergenerational repayment image without harmonizing it with chapter 31.
Preserves all flesh and the question echoing Jeremiah's own declaration.
Preserves both sons and daughters and the denial of divine command; a note explains the passing-over sacrifice idiom.
